method: One record per supplied paragraph, bullet (including nested bullets), fenced table or note; normalized text hashes provide stable IDs. No EXE behavior is inferred from release notes.

historical_archive.role: Unchanged original archive through 0.92.0; later releases are supplied in CHANGELOG.md.

policy.claim_status: Pending until individual current-target evidence and the live source consumer are reviewed. Release-level implemented status is never inherited.
policy.review_store: Claim-specific reviews are durable inputs keyed by stable claim ID and exact target hash. Historical reviews are retained unapplied; changed current review references require reassessment. No review status certifies runtime or complete parity.
policy.supersession: Earlier values are historical leads, never instructions to restore them. Mixed claims require aspect-level review; unknown applicability stays explicit.
policy.scope: Engine, UI, input and platform claims are retained even when outside the native game-mode backlog. Browser/Linux claims require the corresponding artifact before parity can be established.
policy.system_mapping: Release contexts and individual pending ownership reviews provide ownership leads only; system membership does not establish native recovery or source connection.
policy.coverage_gap: Gap #41 tracks incomplete discovery and claim accounting; it does not assert a separate gameplay defect for every supplied claim.
policy.limits: Static accounting does not establish exhaustive EXE discovery, compilation, gameplay, UI/UX, audio or platform parity.

entries.text: Your demons spread out over the horde instead of all piling onto one enemy. They go first for what is closing in on you, gang up on elites and bosses, and leave an enemy alone once enough of them are on it or a missile is about to finish it. Each kind also picks targets its own way: the Felhunter goes for the wounded and the cursed, the Voidwalker guards you, the Succubus and the cleaving demons go where enemies are packed, the Doomguard goes for the toughest, and the Imp aims at enemies not yet burning with Immolate. Melee demons surround their target instead of standing in one spot.

entries.text: Every boss now fights with real raid mechanics: it stops to cast, and the ground shows exactly where the blow will land, filling up until it strikes. Get out of circles, cones and lines, get in close under donuts, dodge waves that march across the room, and stand in the blue towers when they fill. Bosses change their tactics as their health drops, and tell you so.

entries.text: Every boss now has a signature of its own, and every guardian fights its own way instead of all of them charging and stomping alike. New mechanics join the ground markers: knockbacks, eggs that hatch, totems and wards that shield or heal their boss, orbs that chase you, tethers to break, a gaze you must not move under, shockwaves to step through, burning ground, dance lanes, bombs to carry into the horde, crystals that weaken a boss, and bosses that change their stance mid-fight. Every mechanic can be handled in melee range, and the fights are a little harder than before.

entries.text: A big warlock balance pass: your demons now attack faster with your cooldown reduction, the Felguard and the Pit Lord come on their own every 30 seconds or sooner (two at once at high cooldown reduction), and Legion Gate sends three random demons every 4 seconds. Felhunters, Succubi, Voidwalkers, the Doomguard and Demonic Supremacy all play differently, and the Destruction and Affliction trees have moved a few talents. Eleven bosses also have a new achievement with a reward, among them a Defias Bandana every class can wear as a look.

entries.text: Legion Gate: every 4 sec, 3 lesser demons come, the first ones 4 sec into the run. Each wave stays 16 sec and the next 12 sec, in turn, so once it is going you have 12 out, then 9, then 12 again. Each one is an Imp, a Succubus or your companion's kind at random: Felhunters with Soul Devourer, Voidwalkers with Soul Link, never the other (three of the same can happen). Up to 12 at once; your own Imp and companion don't count. Before, it favoured Imps and your companion's kind.

entries.text: Felhunter: Consume Magic replaces its critical strikes on cursed enemies, its bonus damage to them and Soul Fracture; its bites now grow only with how wounded their target is: 0.5/1/2% more damage for every 1% of health it is missing, by Soul Devourer's rank (was 0.75/1.5/3%). Each bite takes 10% of what is left of your highest-ranked damage over time on its target (Curse of Agony, Corruption, Immolate or Drain Life, whichever of your spells has the highest rank), which then ends 10% sooner, and deals 150% of that damage at once. No Felhunter feeds on the same enemy again for 3 sec.
